review_comment: I think if this is important enough to test, we should make it an exception not an assertion. Assertions are not always enabled so this could slip through. What do you think?

If I correctly understand, asserts are more to enforce that the developer is doing the correct thing (generate valid states of the system by code), and exceptions, to say like "Hey the system state is not valid due to the user input". In this case, the merge of 2 `ScriptContextStats` is only made by the developer, so that's why I used an assert :P .

Hm, that is true about assertions, but I think exceptions are not limited to user input they can be more generic to also catch and describe an unexpected situation. In any case, we can leave the assertion as is.
